BANGKOK, Thailand (CNN)  -- At least 59 people were killed and more than 200 others injured early Thursday after a fire broke out at an upscale Bangkok nightclub where about 1,000 revelers were ringing in the new year, Thai police said. Rescue officials survey the scene of the nightclub fire in Bangkok, Thailand. Most of the victims died from smoke inhalation or were trampled in a rush to get out of the club. Thirty bodies have been identified: 29 Thai nationals and one Singaporean, according to police. The fire began at the nightclub Santika about 12:35 a.m., police said. Rescue officials said 226 others were injured, including several foreigners. Two Americans were injured in the blaze, a U.S. State Department official said. The official did not release the victims' names or the extent of their injuries but said the department was in contact with them. Steven Hall, a British national who was hurt in the fire, told CNN that flames began to spread along the ceiling above the stage where a band and DJ were performing. But some people appeared to believe that it was part of the performance. "At the same time there were people rushing to get out, there were other people who seemed to be lacking a sense of urgency and didn't seem to realize what was going on," Hall said. The blaze started near a stage where fireworks were being used as part of a performance on the club's closing night, said police Maj. Gen. Chokchai Deeprasertwit.   Watch the fire engulf the building » . "It may have been caused from sparks, but we don't know if it was sparks from guests or from the nightclub's countdown display on the nightclub stage," he said. iReport.com: Eyewitness captures scene of deadly aftermath . Hall said his wife escaped ahead of him, but he got caught in a crowd. "The lights went out, and at that moment, my back started burning, and I was breathing in hot air," he said.  Watch Steven Hall describe his experience » . British citizen Andrew Jones said he was celebrating in the area when he walked up on the fire. He said he saw victims being rushed out on stretchers and spoke to witnesses, including a fellow Briton who saw fireworks being lit onstage. "He immediately ran out of the building, but immediately when he'd done that, the lights went out, and he couldn't see," Jones said. The club is in one of Bangkok's busiest commercial districts. Its Web site features images of bands and DJs performing on both indoor and outdoor stages, and says that it "innovatively blends the comfort of nature with the excitement of the Bangkok nightlife." The site advertises the club's New Year's party, which was named "Goodbye Santika." CNN's Kocha Olarn contributed to this report.

“The lights went out, and at that moment, my back started burning, and I was breathing in hot air,” he said.

**Deadly fire tears through Bangkok nightclub during New Year’s celebration**

**BANGKOK, Thailand —** A fast-moving fire swept through a packed Bangkok nightclub during New Year’s celebrations early Thursday, killing at least **59 people** and injuring more than **200 others**, Thai officials said.

The blaze broke out shortly after midnight at the **Santika Club**, a popular venue in the city’s upscale **Ekkamai** district, as hundreds of revelers were celebrating the arrival of the new year.

Police and rescue workers said many victims were trapped inside as flames and thick smoke filled the building. Some died from burns, while others were believed to have suffocated or been crushed as panicked crowds rushed for the exits.

Witnesses described scenes of chaos as partygoers tried to escape.

“There was fire everywhere, and people were screaming,” one survivor said. “Everyone ran to the door, but it was too crowded.”

Another witness said sparks appeared near the stage area moments before the fire spread rapidly through the club. Authorities were investigating whether **fireworks or pyrotechnics used during the countdown celebration** may have ignited the blaze.

Bangkok police officials said the club was crowded at the time of the fire, with estimates ranging from several hundred to about 1,000 people inside. Investigators were examining the club’s safety systems, emergency exits and whether the venue had proper authorization for pyrotechnic displays.

Police said the dead included both Thai nationals and foreigners. Among the injured were visitors from several countries, including **Australia, Japan, Nepal and the Netherlands**, according to hospital and official reports.

Rescue workers carried victims from the charred building through the early morning hours. The front of the club was blackened, and parts of the interior appeared heavily damaged by fire.

Officials said the casualty count could rise as hospitals continued treating severely burned victims. Police said they were questioning club staff, witnesses and organizers of the New Year’s event as part of the investigation.

The Santika Club was well known among Bangkok’s nightlife crowd and was reportedly hosting one of its final parties before closing.

**Dozens Killed as Fire Sweeps Through Upscale Bangkok Nightclub During New Year’s Celebration**

**BANGKOK, Thailand** — A New Year’s celebration turned into a scene of panic and death early Thursday when a fast-moving fire tore through an upscale Bangkok nightclub packed with about 1,000 revelers, killing dozens of people and injuring scores more, Thai police said.

The blaze erupted shortly after midnight at the **Santika Club**, a popular nightspot in Bangkok’s Ekkamai district, as patrons were celebrating the arrival of the new year. Witnesses described flames racing through the club as partygoers, many of them dressed for the holiday celebration, rushed toward exits amid thick smoke, falling debris and confusion.

Thai police said the club was crowded at the time of the fire, with approximately 1,000 people inside. Authorities said they were investigating whether fireworks or pyrotechnics used during the celebration may have ignited flammable materials inside the building.

British survivor **Steven Hall** described the scene as chaotic and terrifying.

“People were screaming and trying to get out,” Hall said, recalling how the festive atmosphere changed within moments. He said smoke quickly filled the venue, making it difficult to see and breathe as the crowd surged toward the doors.

Hall said many inside initially did not understand the danger, believing the flames might be part of the show. But panic spread as the fire intensified.

“It was just mayhem,” he said. “Everyone was pushing, everyone was trying to escape.”

Police and rescue officials said many victims were trapped inside the club as flames engulfed parts of the building. Some died from burns, while others were overcome by smoke or crushed in the rush to escape.

Emergency crews arrived to find injured patrons outside the venue, some with severe burns, others suffering from smoke inhalation. Ambulances ferried victims to hospitals across Bangkok as firefighters worked to bring the blaze under control.

Thai police said investigators were examining the club’s safety systems, including emergency exits, fire extinguishers and whether the venue had the proper permits for pyrotechnic effects. Officials also said they were interviewing staff, survivors and witnesses to determine how the fire started and why so many people were unable to escape quickly.

The Santika Club was known as an upscale destination for young Thais, expatriates and tourists. The New Year’s Eve event was heavily attended, with live music and a countdown celebration continuing past midnight.

Survivors said the fire appeared to spread rapidly near the stage area, where a band had been performing. Moments later, flames and smoke swept across the crowded interior.

Hall said the crowd’s desperation grew as visibility worsened.

“You couldn’t see where you were going,” he said. “People were falling. People were climbing over each other.”

Authorities said the death toll could rise as hospitals continued treating the injured. Police urged families searching for missing relatives to contact emergency centers set up after the blaze.

The tragedy prompted renewed scrutiny of fire safety standards at Bangkok entertainment venues, particularly clubs hosting large crowds during holiday events. Thai officials said a full investigation was under way.
